name: 15b bpe merges
title: Byte pair encoding merges the most frequent adjacent pair
subtitle: Corpus: low x5, lower x2, lowest x3, newest x6; pairs are counted inside words, weighted by word count

steps.caption: Training starts with every word split into characters, so the vocabulary is the 8 letters l, o, w, e, r, s, t, n. Each round counts every adjacent pair, weighting by how often the word appears.
Round 1: w+e occurs 11 times, more than any other pair. It becomes the new symbol "we" and every occurrence in the corpus is rewritten.
Round 2: l+o occurs 10 times, more than any other pair. It becomes the new symbol "lo" and every occurrence in the corpus is rewritten.
Round 3: we+s occurs 9 times, more than any other pair. It ties with s+t, and the pair seen first in the corpus wins. It becomes the new symbol "wes" and every occurrence in the corpus is rewritten.
Round 4: wes+t occurs 9 times, more than any other pair. It becomes the new symbol "west" and every occurrence in the corpus is rewritten.
Round 5: n+e occurs 6 times, more than any other pair. It ties with e+west, and the pair seen first in the corpus wins. It becomes the new symbol "ne" and every occurrence in the corpus is rewritten.
Round 6: ne+west occurs 6 times, more than any other pair. It becomes the new symbol "newest" and every occurrence in the corpus is rewritten.
Round 7: lo+w occurs 5 times, more than any other pair. It becomes the new symbol "low" and every occurrence in the corpus is rewritten.
After 7 merges the vocabulary has 8 + 7 = 15 symbols. "low" and "newest" are single tokens, "lowest" is lo + west, and "lower" is lo + we + r. The pieces follow frequency, not meaning.
The word "slowest" never appeared in training. Encoding starts from its characters, s l o w e s t, and tries each learned merge in the order it was learned.
steps.heading: Encoding replays the merge list in training order

steps.caption: Merge 5, n+e: no adjacent n followed by e, so nothing changes.

steps.caption: Merge 6, ne+west: no adjacent ne followed by west, so nothing changes.
steps.heading: Encoding replays the merge list in training order

steps.caption: Merge 7, lo+w: no adjacent lo followed by w, so nothing changes. Merge 7 cannot fire because merge 1 already joined w to e, which is why order matters.
